title: House Appropriations Subcommittee Proposes 46% Cut to LSC Funding
author: Legal Services Corporation

dom.t: LSC funding: Preservation came with reduced resources

It appropriately treats the House and White House figures as pending proposals rather than enacted outcomes, although its service-loss and economic-return claims remain advocacy-based predictions or aggregate estimates.

kp.k: Proposed FY 2026 funding cuts threaten civil legal aid
kp.d: LSC's July 15, 2025 press release reports a House subcommittee proposal to appropriate $300 million for FY 2026, compared with $560 million in FY 2025: a $260 million reduction described as a 46% cut. These are proposed, not enacted, changes. The document addresses civil legal aid funding and access to justice rather than AI.
qs: The House of Representatives Appropriations Subcommittee included $300 million in funding for the Legal Services Corporation (LSC) today in their proposed Commerce, Justice, Science and Related Agencies (CJS) Fiscal Year 2026 appropriations legislation.
This represents a 46% cut from LSC’s FY 2025 funding level of $560 million.

kp.k: LSC projects millions fewer people receiving assistance
kp.d: Conditional on enactment, LSC projects over 2.9 million fewer Americans receiving civil legal help, including nearly 454,000 children, nearly 144,000 older Americans aged 60+, over 20,000 veterans and over 94,000 domestic violence survivors. These are projected service losses, not observed outcomes; the release does not explain the calculation methodology.
qs: If enacted, this $260 million reduction in LSC’s funding would mean that **nearly 3 million fewer Americans would receive legal assistance.**

**Over 2.9 million fewer Americans** would receive civil legal help - **Nearly 454,000 fewer children** would be assisted - **Nearly 144,000 fewer older Americans (age 60+)** would be served - **Over 20,000 fewer veterans** would be supported - **Over 94,000 fewer survivors of domestic violence **would be protected

kp.k: House proposal differs from White House elimination proposal
kp.d: The release contrasts the House proposal with the White House's May 30 FY 2026 budget proposal to eliminate LSC, which included $21 million for closure. It reports that full committee markup had been postponed without a rescheduled date, leaving the appropriations outcome unresolved.
qs: to eliminate LSC in its FY 2026 budget proposal to Congress on May 30, which provided $21 million to close down LSC.
The full committee markup of the House appropriations bill has been postponed and not yet rescheduled.

kp.k: Funding rollback accompanies increased eligibility for legal aid
kp.d: LSC says the proposed funding level would return the organization to its 1999 funding level despite growth in income-eligible Americans from 45.6 million in 1999 to over 52.3 million currently. The release additionally characterizes the reduction as an over 60% cut when adjusted for inflation, without detailing that calculation.
qs: The proposed 46% cut would take LSC back to the organization’s 1999 funding level despite increased need for legal help in the decades since.
In 1999, 45.6 million Americans’ household incomes made them eligible for LSC-funded services.
Currently, over 52.3 million Americans are eligible for LSC-funded legal assistance.
When adjusted for inflation, a $260 million dollar reduction would actually represent an over 60% cut to LSC’s funding.

kp.k: LSC leadership warns of diminished access to justice
kp.d: LSC President Ron Flagg argues that the proposed cut would severely restrict assistance for people unable to afford lawyers and threaten over 25 years of access-to-justice progress. His expectation that congressional bipartisan support might protect funding is expressed as hope, not a forecast supported by an appropriations decision.
qs: “The proposed cut to LSC would severely limit the ability of LSC-funded legal services to assist everyday Americans who are faced with devastating legal problems but cannot afford an attorney,” said LSC President Ron Flagg.
“We are deeply concerned by the prospect of rolling back over 25 years of progress in increasing access to justice across the country,” Flagg continued.

kp.k: Funding support spans legislators and legal-sector stakeholders
kp.d: The release reports funding-support letters endorsed by 48 bipartisan senators and 154 bipartisan House members, alongside letters from 40 bipartisan state attorneys general, 37 bipartisan state supreme court chief justices, leaders of 160 U.S. law firms and general counsels or chief legal officers of 104 major corporations. These demonstrate reported advocacy for funding, not legislative commitments or enacted appropriations.
qs: This year, “Dear Colleague” letters in support of robust funding for LSC were endorsed by 48 bipartisan members of the U.S. Senate and 154 bipartisan members of the U.S. House of Representatives.

kp.k: Federal appropriations primarily fund independent nonprofit service providers
kp.d: LSC reports distributing more than 94% of its federal appropriation through grants to 130 independent nonprofits with offices in every congressional district. Their work includes representation, resources and education concerning domestic violence, disaster recovery, consumer scams and fraud, and housing.
qs: More than 94% of LSC’s federal appropriation is distributed as grants to 130 independent nonprofit organizations with offices in every Congressional district around the country.

These organizations provide direct representation, resources and education to their communities for civil legal matters involving domestic violence, disaster recovery, consumer scams and fraud, housing and more.

kp.k: LSC requests $2.13 billion to meet annual demand
kp.d: LSC's FY 2026 request sought $2.13 billion, unanimously approved by its bipartisan board. The organization bases that request on its assessment of resources required to fully serve the 3.7 million eligible Americans who seek assistance annually; this is a stated funding-needs assessment rather than an enacted allocation.
qs: called for $2.13 billion to fund this work.

This funding request, which was unanimously approved by the organization’s bipartisan Board of Directors, is based on the resources needed for LSC-funded legal services providers to fully serve the 3.7 million eligible Americans who seek assistance each year.

kp.k: Reported research links legal aid to economic returns
kp.d: The release cites an analysis of over 50 studies reporting an average return of $7 per $1 invested in civil legal services. It attributes economic benefits to preventing problems that generate emergency medical, law-enforcement and shelter costs, and to improved family stability, increased local economic participation and reduced reliance on assistance. It does not provide individual study designs, periods or methodological qualifications.
qs: Recent analysis of over 50 studies found that civil legal services yield an average return of [$7 for every $1 invested](http://www.lsc.gov/roi).

Legal assistance generates a positive economic impact by preventing or solving legal problems that would lead to costly public expenditures on things like emergency medical care, law enforcement and shelters.
Legal aid also helps improve family stability, leading to increased participation in local economies and reduced reliance on other forms of assistance.
